title: Universal lifting from a multiplicatively simply connected group
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. All groups are smooth connected affine $F$-group schemes of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and subgroup schemes are closed [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Call a homomorphism a multiplicative isogeny if it is faithfully flat and its scheme-theoretic kernel is finite, central and diagonalizable. Faithfully flat means that the induced map of coordinate algebras makes extension of scalars exact and detects zero modules. Finite means that the coordinate algebra is finite dimensional over $F$; central means commuting with all group elements after every algebra extension; diagonalizable means isomorphic to $D_F(M)=\operatorname{Spec}F[M]$ for a finite abelian group $M$, with basis $e_m$, multiplication $e_me_n=e_{m+n}$ and comultiplication $e_m\mapsto e_m\otimes e_m$. Let $H$ be multiplicatively simply connected: every multiplicative isogeny $H_1\to H$ from a smooth connected affine group of finite type is an isomorphism. For any two multiplicative isogenies $q:H\to G$ and $p:E\to G$, there is a unique group-scheme homomorphism $u:H\to E$ such that $p\circ u=q$. Kernels need not be reduced.

source.place: Definition 18.5, Proposition 18.6(a), Definition 18.7 and Proposition 18.8, printed pp.388--389; algebraically closed fields are perfect.

proof.text: Put $K=\ker p$ and form $P=H\times_G E$, with projections $a:P\to H$ and $b:P\to E$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Componentwise multiplication and inverse make $P$ a group scheme: for every $F$-algebra $A$, its points are the pairs $(h,e)$ satisfying $q(h)=p(e)$, and this condition is preserved by those operations [def-sc-group-scheme]. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $F[P]=F[H]\otimes_{F[G]}F[E]$. It is generated over $F$ by the images of finite sets of algebra generators for $F[H]$ and $F[E]$, hence $P$ is affine of finite type. By [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-base-change], $a^*:F[H]\to F[P]$ is faithfully flat. The kernel of $a$ is scheme-theoretically $K$, via $e\mapsto(1,e)$; this follows from the same equations on points over every algebra. It is central in $P$, since $K$ is central in $E$. No smoothness or reducedness of $P$ is asserted.

source.place: Proposition 18.8, printed p.389, pullback construction; affine computation: Stacks Tags 01I4 and 01JQ; faithful-flat base change: Tags 00HI and 00HQ.

proof.text: Let $C=P^0$ have its open-subscheme structure. By [lem-sfb-group-neutral-component-translates], $C$ is an open and closed subgroup, and $|P|$ is the disjoint union of finitely many translates $g_iC$, with $g_i\in P(F)$. By [lem-sfb-locally-algebraic-group-identity-component], $R=C_{\mathrm{red}}$ is a smooth connected group scheme of finite type and has the same underlying space as $C$. Its inclusion $j:R\to P$ is closed: $C\to P$ is closed, and reduction is a closed subscheme. On affine coordinates these inclusions are quotient maps [def-weil-closed-immersion], so $R$ is affine. Put $r=a\circ j$. In particular the finitely many closed translates of $|R|$ cover $|P|$.

source.place: Proposition 18.6(a), printed p.388; Propositions 1.34, 1.38 and Corollary 1.39, pp.16--18; Stacks Tags 0B7R and 047R.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homomorphism-factorization] to $r:R\to H$. Both groups are affine and hence separated: the diagonal on affine coordinates is induced by the surjection $A\otimes_F A\to A$, $x\otimes y\mapsto xy$. The factorization gives a closed subgroup $I\hookrightarrow H$ with $|I|=r(|R|)$, because its first map is surjective. By [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum] applied to $a^*$, $a$ is surjective on underlying spaces. Thus $|H|$ is the finite union of the closed translates $a(g_i)|I|$: on $g_iR$, the homomorphism $a$ is translation by $a(g_i)$ followed by $r$. Since $H$ is connected, its identity component is all of $H$; [lem-sfb-locally-algebraic-group-identity-component] makes $H$ geometrically irreducible, hence irreducible. An irreducible space covered by finitely many closed subsets equals one of them (induct on the number of subsets using the definition of irreducibility). Therefore one translate of $|I|$ is $|H|$, and translating back gives $|I|=|H|$. Consequently $r$ is surjective.

source.place: Expansion of the assertion that the reduced neutral component maps onto the connected target in Proposition 18.6(a), p.388, using the Homomorphism Theorem 5.39, p.108 and components/translations of 1.34--1.35, pp.16--17.

proof.text: The scheme $H$ is reduced by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced], applied to its smooth structure morphism over $F$. Surjectivity of $r$ implies that $r^*:F[H]\to F[R]$ is injective: if $r^*(f)=0$, then $f$ belongs to every prime of $F[H]$, since each such prime is the inverse image of a prime of $F[R]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq] for the zero ideal, $f$ is nilpotent and is zero by reducedness. This is a homomorphism of finitely generated commutative Hopf $F$-algebras, since $r$ is a group-scheme homomorphism. The reduced-target theorem [lem-sfb-reduced-target-dominant-group-flatness] therefore says exactly that $r^*$ is faithfully flat, in the coordinate-algebra sense required in the statement.

source.place: Proposition 18.6(a), p.388; the faithful-flatness justification is Corollary 1.69 and Proposition 1.70, p.28; reducedness: Stacks Tag 056T.

proof.text: By the kernel fibre-product description, $L=\ker r=R\times_P K$ is a closed subgroup of $K=\ker a$. Indeed it is obtained by pulling back the closed inclusion $R\hookrightarrow P$; on coordinates its algebra is a quotient of $F[K]$, so it is finite dimensional [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For every $F$-algebra $A$, its elements commute with $R(A)$ since their images in $P(A)$ lie in the central subgroup $K(A)$. Thus $L$ is central in $R$, scheme-theoretically. Write $K\simeq D_F(M)$ as in the hypothesis, and choose generators $m_1,\ldots,m_t$ of the finite abelian group $M$ (allow $t=0$ when $M=0$). Sending $z_i$ to $e_{m_i}$ defines a surjection $F[z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_t^{\pm1}]\to F[M]$, compatible with all Hopf operations, and hence a closed group immersion $K\hookrightarrow\mathbf G_m^t$. The composite embeds $L$ as a finite closed subgroup of this split torus. By [lem-sfb-split-torus-subgroups-diagonalizable], $L\simeq D_F(N)$ for a finite abelian group $N$. Together with steps 2 and 4, this proves that $r:R\to H$ is a multiplicative isogeny.

source.place: Proposition 18.6(a), p.388, kernel of the restricted map; Theorem 12.9(c), printed pp.233--234 (closed subgroups of diagonalizable groups).

proof.text: By the stated simple-connectedness hypothesis on $H$, the multiplicative isogeny $r:R\to H$ is an isomorphism. Its inverse is a group homomorphism: applying the injective map $r$ to the proposed multiplication identity reduces it to that for $r$. Let $u=b\circ j\circ r^{-1}:H\to E$. The pullback identity $p\circ b=q\circ a$ gives $p\circ u=q\circ r\circ r^{-1}=q$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. This constructs the required lift.

source.place: Proposition 18.6(a), p.388, inverse of the restricted isogeny; Proposition 18.8, p.389, composition with the second projection.

proof.text: For uniqueness, let $v:H\to E$ also satisfy $p\circ v=q$. Multiplication and inversion define a scheme morphism $\delta:H\to E$, $h\mapsto u(h)v(h)^{-1}$, with $p\circ\delta=1$; hence it factors through $K=\ker p$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-zero-dim-local-discrete-spectrum] with base ring $F$ and finite algebra $F[K]$, $|K|$ is finite discrete. The continuous image of the connected space $|H|$ in this discrete space is a singleton: inverse images of any chosen point and its complement would otherwise separate $H$. As both homomorphisms preserve identity, that singleton is the identity point. The unit $e_K:\operatorname{Spec}F\to K$ is a closed immersion: on coordinates its counit is surjective, since it splits the inclusion of constants [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The source $H$ is reduced by step 4. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme] applied to this unit makes $\delta$ factor through $\operatorname{Spec}F$, so $\delta=e_K$ as a scheme morphism. For every $F$-algebra $A$ and every $h\in H(A)$, this says $u(h)v(h)^{-1}=1$, and thus $u=v$. This proves equality on all algebra-valued points, including in positive characteristic with nonreduced $K$.

source.place: Proposition 18.8, p.389, uniqueness; expanded scheme-theoretically using Stacks Tag 0356 and the finite-spectrum facts in the proof of Tag 06RS (Tags 05DR and 00GT).
